applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 8 (often about ages 13-14) onto that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Florida Grade 8 social studies is grade-based American history through Reconstruction, civics, economics, financial literacy, geography, and one history-of-communism benchmark (SS.8). The shared Grades 6-8 band (SS.68.AA and SS.68.HE, 15 benchmarks) lives only in the grade-7 Florida file. It is not copied into this grade and is not aligned again here. Those codes are not IB learning outcomes.

subject_group_or_structure.mapping_to_primer_subject: Grade 8 Florida social studies (SS.8 American history, civics, economics, financial literacy, geography, and history of communism) is mapped here to MYP individuals and societies. The public page allows discrete courses such as history, geography, economics, and civics, or an integrated humanities course. It does not require this Florida list. The SS.68 band is not part of this mapping.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Developing and applying these social, thinking, research, communication and self management skills helps students learn how to learn.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP prescribes sixteen key interdisciplinary concepts along with related concepts for each discipline.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: MYP teachers assess the prescribed subject-group objectives using the assessment criteria for each subject group in each year of the programme.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Individuals and societies incorporates disciplines traditionally studied in the humanities, as well as disciplines in the social sciences.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: In this subject group, students collect, describe and analyse data used in studies of societies, test hypotheses, and learn how to interpret complex information, including original source material.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Schools can organize the study of individuals and societies in the MYP as discrete courses, modular courses, or integrated courses. Discrete-course examples named on the page include history, geography, economics, and civics.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The individuals and societies subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Knowing and understanding; B Investigating; C Communicating; D Thinking critically. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 8 Florida social studies in this draft is American history from British colonial settlement through the Civil War and Reconstruction, plus civics of that era, economics, a long financial-literacy sequence, geography of the United States in American history, and one benchmark on early communal living. MYP individuals and societies asks students to investigate societies and to use sources. It does not set the Florida document list, the financial-literacy sequence, or a Grade 8 placement. SS.68 African American History and Holocaust Education stay in the grade-7 file only. This grade does not align them again.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Using text, oral history, and a check on validity can sit under criterion B Investigating. Those source rules are Florida's.
The Constitutional Convention and the named compromises can be studied in a history course under criterion A. That list is Florida content, not an IB objective.
The rule of law in the United States' constitutional republic is a Florida civics benchmark. The public MYP page names civics as a possible discrete course, not this sentence.
How the Bill of Rights guarantees civil rights and liberties is a Florida civics benchmark. The public MYP pages do not name those amendments.
Scarcity, supply and demand, opportunity costs, incentives, and profits fit economics, which the page names as a possible discipline. Those factors in this sentence are Florida's.
Interest as the price of using a saver's money is Florida financial literacy. The public MYP pages name economics. They do not publish this personal-finance sequence.
Migration to and within the United States fits geography as a possible course and the example key concept of time, place and space. The American-history frame is Florida's.

Examining early communal living and its effect on economic stability is a Florida History of Communism benchmark. The public MYP pages retrieved do not name communal living. This row does not turn that sentence into an IB outcome.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
